title: IGC-Net for conditional average potential outcome estimation over time
claim: Fully regression-based iterative G-computation can be realized as a neural end-to-end architecture with shared components and blocked gradients across generation and learning steps.
layout: Single wide panel, top-to-bottom layers, repeated columns, legend at bottom
description: A wide architecture diagram arranged as horizontal dashed bands stacked top to bottom: Data, Neural backbone, Hidden states and treatment, G-computation heads, and learning targets. The top row shows circles for the history, interventional treatments (green) and observational treatments (blue), covariates and outcomes (grey). Dense arrows run from the data down to double-bordered boxes z^φ (the backbone), which are green for the generation step and blue for the learning step and linked by 'Same component' labels. Diamonds hold hidden states Z. The g^φ heads below produce the G-tilde diamonds. Red double bars mark blocked gradients, and 'Learn' links join the blue expectation diamonds to the green targets. A yellow box marks the CAPO estimate, and the final target is Y_{t+τ}. A boxed legend at the bottom explains the symbols and colors.
caption: Iterative G-computation network. Neural endto-end architecture of our iterative G-computation network.
abstract: Estimating potential outcomes for treatments over time based on observational data is important for personalized decision-making in medicine. However, many existing methods for this task fail to properly adjust for time-varying confounding and thus yield biased estimates. There are only a few neural methods with proper adjustments, but these have inherent limitations (e.g., division by propensity scores that are often close to zero), which result in poor performance. As a remedy, we introduce the iterative G-computation network (IGC-Net). Our IGC-Net is a novel, neural end-to-end model which adjusts for time-varying confounding in order to estimate conditional average potential outcomes (CAPOs) over time. Specifically, our IGC-Net is the first neural model to perform fully regression-based iterative G-computation for CAPOs in the time-varying setting. We evaluate the effectiveness of our IGC-Net across various experiments. In sum, this work represents a significant step towards personalized decision-making from electronic health records.
